subject.title: [Feature]: Native E2EE Browser Chat, No Third-Party Required

question: Should OpenClaw pursue native no-third-party browser-held E2EE chat as a Gateway/WebChat capability, define Gateway/plugin seams for an external encrypted browser transport first, or defer this direction in favor of existing encrypted channel and WebChat/Tailscale paths?
rationale: The request changes encryption trust boundaries, browser-held key ownership, transcript visibility, relay fallback, and core-versus-plugin ownership; automation cannot choose those security and product boundaries safely.

options.title: Approve design-first Gateway capability
options.body: Define the threat model, encrypted envelope protocol, key lifecycle, transcript semantics, and Gateway/Control UI contracts before any implementation branch.

options.title: Make it plugin-first
options.body: Keep core lean by adding only the missing Gateway/plugin SDK seams needed for an external encrypted browser transport to integrate safely.

options.title: Defer native transport
options.body: Keep WebChat/Tailscale plus Matrix, Nostr, Signal, and dmScope isolation as the supported paths unless maintainers later sponsor this direction.

recommendation.title: Approve design-first Gateway capability
recommendation.body: Define the threat model, encrypted envelope protocol, key lifecycle, transcript semantics, and Gateway/Control UI contracts before any implementation branch.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is primarily the encryption/key ownership, browser trust, relay, and transcript-visibility boundary before WebChat product shape can be finalized.
